**A golden evaluation set is a versioned collection of representative inputs, expected behavior, and scoring rules.** “Golden” means curated and maintained; it does not mean the labels are infallible or the set permanently represents production. [1](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/)

For a support assistant, include answerable questions, missing-information cases, outdated documents, ambiguous requests, and requests requiring abstention. Each item should state what a successful response must contain, what would be unacceptable, and which evidence supports the expected answer. Exact string equality is often inappropriate for equivalent natural-language answers.

Define the rubric before comparing model outputs. Separate factual correctness, completeness, citation support, formatting, and task-specific constraints. A response can be fluent but unsupported, or correct but unusable because it violates a required output schema. Combining everything into one score too early hides the reason for regressions. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685)[3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15217)

Version the input, reference evidence, labels, rubric, and evaluator. When a source document changes, decide whether the expected answer should change too. Otherwise a more current answer can be incorrectly marked wrong. Keep examples used for prompt development separate from the final held-out evaluation.

**Sampling matters.** A set containing only memorable failures is useful as a regression suite but cannot estimate average production quality without an appropriate sampling design. Maintain both representative samples and intentionally difficult slices. Report each slice separately, and label any weighted aggregate with the population weights used.

For subjective scoring, have independent annotators label a subset and examine disagreements. If an LLM judge is used, calibrate it against human decisions, test order and verbosity biases, and preserve its version and prompt. Finally, retain per-example results so a change in the overall score can be traced to concrete cases. The useful artifact is a reproducible decision process, not merely a spreadsheet of questions. [1](https://research.google/pubs/the-ml-test-score-a-rubric-for-ml-production-readiness-and-technical-debt-reduction/)[2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685)[4](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/model_evaluation.html)
